report.subtitle: Automated post-hazard building damage assessment
report.verdictRule: The verdict is the class of the region the detector scored highest; a tie goes to the more severe class. Each box on the photograph is graded on its own, so one photograph can carry regions of different severity.
report.scoresNote: Highest detector confidence per class — independent maxima, not probabilities that sum to 100%.

report.generatedBy: Generated by DamageScale — AI structural damage assessment (demo)

scale.title: The four destruction classes
scale.intro: The trained model locates buildings and reports the class it detected with the highest confidence: no damage, slight/moderate, heavy/very heavy, or total damage.

dataset.title: Dataset and labeling
dataset.sourcesBody: The detector was trained on a four-class annotated set of post-hazard building photographs, each image carrying bounding boxes rather than a single whole-image label. Training was configured for 150 epochs at 800px and early-stopped at 55, shipping epoch 25. The labelled set is held by the model author and its per-class composition has not been measured on this machine, so no image counts are published here — an invented breakdown would be worse than none. The earlier PHI-Net Task 5 figures that stood here described the retired classifiers, not this model.
dataset.labelingBody: Every building in an image is boxed and graded independently, which is why one photograph can contain regions of different severity. The four grades map onto this scale in order: no damage, slight/moderate, heavy/very heavy, total. Because each region is graded on its own, the whole-image verdict is not a label the model produces — it is the grade of the region the detector scored highest, so the headline always matches the strongest evidence on the photograph.

model.title: Model architecture
model.body: One detector ships. It is a YOLOv8s network fine-tuned to find every building in a photograph and grade each one against the four destruction classes, trained at 800px on PyTorch through Ultralytics, early-stopped at epoch 55 of a planned 150. Its output is a set of boxes — one class code and one confidence per detected region — not a single label for the whole image.
model.frameworkNote: That is why the verdict on the analyze page is derived rather than predicted: the retained detection with the highest confidence decides it, and within each class the highest detector confidence is reported. The trade-off is stated plainly — a faintly detected collapsed wing beside a confidently detected intact facade reports the facade — so the boxes drawn on the photograph, not the headline alone, carry the full finding. It is also why a photo with no retained detection is reported as no detection, never quietly as no damage.
model.mockNote: A deterministic mock backend remains available for environments without the model weights installed, so the demo still runs anywhere. It is labeled as the mock in the model picker and never impersonates a trained model.

metrics.title: Evaluation metrics
metrics.intro: Measured on the validation split held out from the detector's own training run, and read from the checkpoint that ships.

curves.title: Training curves
curves.intro: Every loss the detector optimises, on both splits, for the whole run. The grey training line keeps falling to the very end, while the amber validation line flattens — and classification loss drifts back upward after epoch 25. That widening gap is the model beginning to fit its training photos rather than the problem, and it is exactly why the run was stopped: no epoch after 25 improved validation mAP@50-95, so the shipped weights are the ones from before the gap opened.
curves.description: {name} on the training and validation splits across {epochs} epochs, with the shipped epoch {bestEpoch} marked.
curves.axisNote: The horizontal axis is the training epoch; the vertical axis is loss, scaled per chart because the three losses have different magnitudes. Loss is what the optimiser minimises, so lower is better — but it is not a score out of anything, and it cannot be compared across models trained on different data.

metrics.earlyStopNote: Training was configured for {plannedEpochs} epochs and stopped early at {epochs}. With a patience of {patience}, no epoch after {bestEpoch} improved validation mAP@50-95, so epoch {bestEpoch} is the checkpoint that ships and every figure above is that epoch's row.
metrics.detectionNote: These are detection metrics, not classification accuracy. The model locates each damaged region and labels it, so it is scored by mean average precision — the overlap between predicted and true regions, averaged across IoU thresholds. A percentage here is not comparable to the top-1 accuracy of an image classifier: mAP is a stricter measure, because a prediction must be both correctly classified and correctly located to count.

gradcam.title: Explainability: where the model looked
gradcam.body: A Grad-CAM heatmap highlights the pixels that most influenced a verdict, turning a bare class label into something an engineer can check. It is not implemented here: the model returns no heatmap, so the analyze page shows none rather than displaying an explanation no model produced.
gradcam.tryNote: The technique itself has to change first. Grad-CAM was built for whole-image classifiers, while a detector already answers where by drawing a box, so explaining why a region earned its grade needs a different method. Until one lands, the <link>analyze page</link> reports the detector confidences alone.
